## Structure and components

- [statement] Foltynie and colleagues describe MDS UPDRS Part 1 as capturing non-motor symptoms, Part 2 as capturing motor impact on daily living, Part 3 as clinician-assessed motor severity, and Part 4 as motor complications. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-08) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13438061/ · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] The EJS ACT-PD registry specifies the equally weighted combined MDS-UPDRS Parts I and II as its primary outcome measuring progression between active-treatment and placebo arms. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-03) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT07207057 · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD

## How it works

- [statement] The EMA guideline states that dopamine uptake or receptor-density imaging is insufficient as a surrogate because correlation with meaningful persistent clinical change has not been established. (low confidence) — https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/scientific-guideline/guideline-clinical-investigation-medicinal-products-treatment-parkinsons-disease_en.pdf-0 · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] McGhee and colleagues warn that an inadequately short wash-out can leave symptomatic carry-over and falsely suggest disease modification. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4910262/ · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] After reviewing wash-in, wash-out, delayed-start and other designs in Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s disease, McGhee and colleagues favour long-term follow-up examining sustained divergence between treatment arms. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4910262/ · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] The LEAP trial authors conclude that levodopa combined with carbidopa had no disease-modifying effect in early Parkinson’s disease over 80 weeks. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30673543/ · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] Stephenson and colleagues report that EMA issued a 2018 Qualification Opinion for DAT imaging as an enrichment biomarker in trials targeting early motor Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6700608/ · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] Mahlknecht and colleagues explain that phenoconversion endpoint events can be increased by selecting higher-risk prodromal participants, extending follow-up, or increasing sample size. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8859908/ · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] The EMA guideline describes milestone-event timing or the proportion reaching a milestone as possible primary endpoints in long-term randomised placebo-controlled disease-progression trials. (low confidence) — https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/scientific-guideline/guideline-clinical-investigation-medicinal-products-treatment-parkinsons-disease_en.pdf-0 · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] The EMA Parkinson’s guideline states that for early untreated Parkinson’s disease the goal is to slow progression of motor symptoms by assessing change in UPDRS, or time to L-Dopa+/DA-agonists, with a trial duration probably up to 24 months. (low confidence) — https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/scientific-guideline/guideline-clinical-investigation-medicinal-products-treatment-parkinsons-disease_en.pdf-0 · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] EMA’s questions-and-answers document on inclusion criteria states that the guideline’s definitions of de novo, early and advanced Parkinson’s disease are working definitions based on clinical practice and not intended to define exact and mutually exclusive patient populations. (low confidence) — https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/scientific-guideline/questions-and-answers-additional-clarification-inclusion-criteria-guideline-clinical-investigation-medicinal-products-treatment-parkinsons-disease-revision-2_en.pdf · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] The same EMA questions-and-answers document states that, because L-dopa is increasingly given as initial treatment, the start of L-dopa therapy is no longer an optimal demarcation criterion between early and more advanced Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/scientific-guideline/questions-and-answers-additional-clarification-inclusion-criteria-guideline-clinical-investigation-medicinal-products-treatment-parkinsons-disease-revision-2_en.pdf · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The EMA Parkinson’s guideline describes improvement of the core symptoms, motor symptoms and activities of daily living, as the endpoint for adjunctive treatment in patients on L-Dopa+ with insufficient control of motor symptoms. (low confidence) — https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/scientific-guideline/guideline-clinical-investigation-medicinal-products-treatment-parkinsons-disease_en.pdf-0 · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] The MDS-UPDRS Motor Examination study used anchor- and distribution-based methods in 260 patients and estimated minimal clinically important changes of -3.25 points for improvement and 4.63 points for worsening. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26578041/ · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] Hauser and colleagues estimated early-Parkinson’s UPDRS III improvement thresholds of −6.2 and −6.1 for pramipexole ER and IR, using patient-rated slight improvement on active treatment minus unchanged placebo participants. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3995302/ · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] The EJS ACT-PD consortium describes interim reviews that continue promising treatments to final efficacy review and stop apparently inactive treatments early, allowing replacement candidates. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.ejsactpd.com/about-us/about-ejs-act-pd-trial/ · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] UCL’s EJS ACT-PD news item states that participants have been randomised to telmisartan, terazosin or a matched placebo, and that the trial is expanding to test ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) as a third potential treatment. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04) — https://www.innovative-ctu.ucl.ac.uk/news/news-stories/2026/november-2026/parkinson-s-trial-ejs-act-pd-adds-a-new-treatment-arm/ · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD
- [statement] UCL reports that EJS ACT-PD had opened at 26 NHS sites across the UK, with more than 189 participants already randomised. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04) — https://www.innovative-ctu.ucl.ac.uk/news/news-stories/2026/november-2026/parkinson-s-trial-ejs-act-pd-adds-a-new-treatment-arm/ · keywords: Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD

## Research summary — Clinical trial design: endpoints, enrichment and platform trials in PD

Parkinson’s trial design separates symptomatic improvement from sustained changes in disease progression. Clinical scales, patient-relevant milestones and carefully defined enrichment strategies serve different purposes. The cited studies illustrate why wash-out and delayed-start findings need cautious interpretation, why clinically important change thresholds depend on the instrument and study method, and why imaging enrichment does not establish a surrogate endpoint. The platform trial combines interim treatment decisions with a registered combined rating-scale primary outcome.
